A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LTKD, with matching objectives, datasets, and many identical results despite the changed title. All supplied pages are readable, and neither PDF contains an appendix. However, v2 references supplementary pseudocode, implementation details, and additional results that are not included, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments on three long-tailed benchmarks, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, and feature visualizations in Tables I–VII and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–6, including a new group-count experiment and the loss-convergence comparison in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The two-component LTKD objective and uniform within-group weighting remain. V2 corrects the specified rebalancing step by explicitly normalizing the scaled group-probability vector in Equation 11, replacing v1's flawed class-level normalization expression. This changes the written procedure; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate long-tailed image classification on CIFAR-100-LT, TinyImageNet-LT, and ImageNet-LT, and retain the balanced-versus-long-tailed CIFAR-100 diagnostic. New group-count experiments and broader application citations do not introduce a new dataset, task, or domain actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes across matched benchmark comparisons. V2 Table 1 replaces CIFAR-100-LT's KD and FitNet rows with DIST and CAT-KD; Table 2 replaces TinyImageNet-LT's FitNet with DIST while retaining KD. ImageNet-LT Table 3 adds DIST and CAT-KD. DKD and ReviewKD remain throughout.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a controlled group-count sweep over 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, and 100 groups for four architecture pairs on CIFAR-100-LT at imbalance factor 100. Existing imbalance factors, balanced testing, accuracy metrics, and the alpha/beta sweep remain. Main tables show fewer architecture configurations, but the unavailable additional results prevent establishing that the full experimental suite contracted.

E4.justification: V2 adds per-group convergence comparisons between KD, DKD, and LTKD in Figure 4 and sensitivity to group granularity in Table 6. Existing component ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity are retained. V1's t-SNE analysis is absent from the supplied v2; whether it appears in the unavailable supplement cannot be checked.

E5.justification: V1 Section IV-B and v2 Section 4.2 both report three repetitions and average performance. Neither supplied PDF reports standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline scores, group-count results, and convergence findings while displaying fewer architecture-result blocks. Most matched scores remain identical, but CIFAR-100-LT ResNet50–MobileNetV2 overall accuracy at imbalance factor 10 changes from 57.46% to 57.79% (Table II to Table 1). V2 also corrects component-ablation tail gains from 7.36/9.19 to 3.70/5.53 percentage points, matching the unchanged underlying table values.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 11 repairs the normalization mathematics: its denominator sums scaled probabilities over groups. V1 Section III-B incorrectly repeats the numerator's scaling factor inside the class summation, causing that factor to cancel. The central KL decomposition and final loss derivation otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The core contributions of decomposing KD, correcting teacher bias, and improving long-tailed accuracy remain. V2 strengthens teacher-surpassing language to 'nearly all cases' in the introduction and explicitly claims to be the first compression-oriented treatment of long-tailed KD in Section 2.2; v1 states the compression focus without that explicit priority claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking teacher bias to suboptimal convergence and group granularity to finer bias correction. It characterizes 100 singleton groups as continuous reweighting and credits discrete grouping with enabling beneficial within-group supervision. The original bias explanation and the head-class suppression tradeoff remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies head, medium, and tail groups as the top 33%, next 34%, and bottom 33% of classes by training frequency. V1's SGD, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005, and dataset-size/resolution details are not repeated in the supplied v2. Its references to supplementary pseudocode and settings cannot establish their contents or an actual optimizer change.

R1.justification: The introduction shifts from general vision architectures and compression techniques toward KD applications across vision, NLP, and language models. Related work adds DIST and several long-tailed distillation references, expands discussion of CAT-KD, and strengthens the compression-oriented novelty claim. Literature coverage and positioning are substantially revised.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Biased Teacher, Balanced Student' to 'Distilling Balanced Knowledge from a Biased Teacher.' The introduction, related work, method exposition, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Inter-/intra-group terminology becomes cross-/within-group, and the contribution narrative is reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview diagrams, restructures and combines benchmark tables, and changes the document formatting. The retained hyperparameter plots move from vertically stacked Figure 4 to side-by-side Figure 5. A convergence figure and group-count table are added, while the t-SNE display is absent from the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical correctness through Equation 11, fixes erroneous ablation-gain arithmetic, and adds useful baseline comparisons and group-count sensitivity evidence. The rewritten exposition also clarifies the method. These are limited net gains: most retained results are unchanged, displayed architecture coverage narrows, and some implementation details available in v1 are absent while the promised supplement is unavailable.
